poor_thing_mishap.description: A short, funny story where a file suffers a common mistake and the narrator pities it. A quick fix ends the scene.
poor_thing_mishap.hook_pattern: Poor [thing], look what people did to it

custom_unboxing_walkthrough.description: Narrator proudly shows a personalised result, such as a finished passport photo or a signed form, and walks through its details.
custom_unboxing_walkthrough.hook_pattern: This video is extra special because I have my own custom [thing]

too_good_to_be_legal_reveal.description: Open with a narrator who says an ordinary-looking tool feels almost illegal. Have a 3D character try it, then stack 3 or 4 quick surprising abilities, each shown in its own panel with a file size or result.
too_good_to_be_legal_reveal.hook_pattern: This [ordinary thing] should be illegal, they should not be selling this

live_disbelief_walkthrough.description: Start with a character who cannot believe something works, then walk through it step by step. The narrator points out small details a viewer would miss, shown on panels.
live_disbelief_walkthrough.hook_pattern: [Hot topic] I just can't believe it, bhai!

playful_rivalry_roast.description: Narrate two tools or habits as friendly rivals, with a cheeky accusation at the start. The 3D characters tease each other and the better tool wins at the end.

festive_refrain_moment.description: Tie one tool to a festive or seasonal deadline moment. The narrator repeats one short line as a refrain while the character finishes the task, then ends on a calm success panel.
festive_refrain_moment.hook_pattern: [Festival/emotion line repeated] with a feeling of arrival

three_things_countdown.description: Have the narrator promise exactly three things a tool does better than people expect. Show each as a big numbered caption on a 3D panel, with a before/after file or size change.
three_things_countdown.hook_pattern: [Famous product] is here, and it has N things [rivals] need to copy

survives_the_torture_test.description: Show a 3D character throwing everything at a file or form (wrong size, locked, corrupted, too big), and the tool still works. The narrator names each trial while the panel shows the error turning into success.
survives_the_torture_test.hook_pattern: This [thing] can survive anything, so even if you do this, this, or this, nothing happens

one_thing_replaces_many.description: Show a character juggling several separate apps or sites for a job, and the narrator reveals a single site that does it all, with the extra apps vanishing from the 3D scene.

two_in_one_claim.description: Open with the first word at 0 s, state that the tool does two jobs people think need two apps, and show both outcomes side by side in two 3D panels.
two_in_one_claim.hook_pattern: This [device] can work like a [A] and a [B]
